text.p: A three-goal spree in the second half propelled Finland to a convincing win over Azerbaijan in Sunday's World Cup European group three qualifier.
The Finnish attack, led by Ajax striker Jari Litmanen, came alive after a messy first half in which the hosts missed a handful of clear chances.
Sami Mahlio forced a diving save from Azerbaijan keeper Alexander Jidkov as early as the fourth minute and Litmanen came close with a powerful long-range shot in the 35th.

But it was Azerbaijan forward Gourban Gourbanov who squandered the clearest chance of the half two minutes later, completely miscueing a perfect pass from captain Ionis Gousseinov with only the goalkeeper to beat.

It took a goalkeeping blunder in the 59th minute to break the deadlock. Finland midfielder Jari Vanhala connected with a long, floated pass from the right wing by defender Jussi Nuorela and Jidkov fumbled his shot, allowing the ball to cross the line.
Finland, fourth in the group above Azerbaijan going into the match, went two ahead five minutes later through a looping Litmanen back-header from inside the box.

Still attacking strongly, Finland put the game beyond Azerbaijan's grasp in the 81st minute after a floundering Jidkov again failed to handle a long pass from Litmanen, giving striker Antti Sumiala an easy knock-in.
